name: Adidas

points.text: Revenue is growing 9.4% year over year (modest).
Earnings changed +58.1% versus a year ago.
Operating margin is 9.2%.
Return on equity is 26.3%.
Debt/equity is 90% (moderate leverage).
Free-cash-flow margin is 6.5% of revenue.
It trades at 14.5x forward earnings.
PEG ratio is 0.66 (price paid per unit of growth).
EV/EBITDA is 11.4x.
Free-cash-flow yield is 6.1%.
Price/sales is only 1.1x.
Price is 9.1% above its 200-day average: the long-term trend is up.
The 50-day average is above the 200-day average (bullish alignment).
RSI(14) is 53: neutral.
MACD is negative and falling: momentum is deteriorating.
It is 9.3% below its 52-week high.
30 Wall Street analysts rate it 1.8/5 on average (buy).
The average analyst price target implies 17.1% upside.
Over 6 months it returned +2.2% versus -1.7% for the MSCI World benchmark.
Last month: +8.3%.
Annualised volatility is 33%.
Worst peak-to-trough fall in the past year: 24.5%.
Beta of 1.13: moves roughly with the market.
No exposure to Consumer Cyclical yet — this would diversify the portfolio.

debate.said: Here is the case for owning Adidas. Earnings changed +58.1% versus a year ago. Return on equity is 26.3%. PEG ratio is 0.66 (price paid per unit of growth).
I'm not convinced. MACD is negative and falling: momentum is deteriorating. Annualised volatility is 33%.
Price action is noise over a few weeks; the business is what we own — earnings changed +58.1% versus a year ago. Weakness can be an entry point.

risk: Maximum position size: 14% of the portfolio (scaled for 33% volatility).
Every order costs a €1 fee, like on Trade Republic. Stop-loss rule: review at -15% from cost.
chair: Weighted committee score is +0.27 on a scale of -1 to +1; 4 of 5 analysts lean the same way. Conviction: Medium.
Decision: BUY. We propose a position of up to 14% of the portfolio.
